purpose: Compare exact three-success ACK pruning against production on delay, independent datagram loss and loopback overload.
method: Persistent daemons within each phase; fresh namespaces between phases. Disjoint CPU placement, no overlapping local builds, kernel tests or Git packing. CPU covers before/sent samples; 100% is one core. Goodput uses receiver sample bytes/time; final missing and counter deltas include two-second drain. Gauges are absolute per-worker after values, never counter deltas. Loopback phase has no netem qdisc. Qdisc-left affects R-to-L; qdisc-right affects L-to-R. Production/candidate/production order. Per-thread context-switch snapshots are retained as raw data.
candidate: Count only exact successfully transmitted ACK snapshots, prune accepted packets after three reports while retaining highest anchor and unchanged duplicate history. Two fixed bitmap planes and a search floor add16408bytes per receive lane. Failed/cancelled submissions do not prune; stale snapshots cannot charge recycled aliases.
disposition: Not accepted alone: repeat60-second delay-only0.5G candidate0.454/0.463 vs production0.471/0.467 and0.466/0.473. Loopback gains remain measured; candidate remains base for separate sender/packing comparisons.
counter_units: Queue drops count source buffers or control records; a dropped GSO source can contain many frames. TAP and socket drops count SKBs, expiry counts frame classes. Do not sum them as exact frame losses.
